look_here_first: Feather fingergrass often forms a TIGHT TERMINAL FAN of about 4–20 radiating, feathery-looking racemes on an annual tuft. Under a lens the fertile lemma typically has a distinctive crown of long apical hairs (about 1.5–4 mm) and a long awn. Current pictures show the feathery head and visible bristly units, NOT a measured isolated fertile lemma or proof of annual crown.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted POWO species with Texas state-level native distribution; approved iNaturalist source pool; project three-county target-zone criterion not independently verified.

morphology_keys.habit: Tufted annual grass of disturbed places with terminal digitate panicle; racemes often 5–10 cm.
morphology_keys.spikelets: Fertile lemma about 2.5–4.2 mm, with long apical marginal hairs (>1.5 mm) and awn about 2.5–15 mm; one or two reduced sterile florets.
best_field_traits: Racemes mostly in one terminal whorl
Conspicuous long hairs on apical fertile lemma margins
crew_field_walkthrough: Photograph the complete terminal fan and central point where long pale racemes join.
Inspect the second closeup for the visible spikelet-bearing rachis and pointed parts; do not assume the points are hairs from a particular lemma.
Expose basal root crown and isolate one mature fertile lemma to demonstrate long apical hairs with mm scale; compare with C. verticillata's whorled architecture.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Entire terminal fan in flowering plant context, noting any lower distinct whorls.
Basal crown with root and nodes showing annual character.
Mature fertile floret at scale with the true crown of 1.5–4 mm hairs.
One or two mature sterile florets and awns, clear separate measurements.
crew_field_steps: Start with the striking densely grouped pale terminal fan in the first picture; the branches rise together near the top.
The second photo shows awnlike projecting structures along a spike-bearing branch. This teaches what to magnify, not a definitive measurement of the fertile-lemma hair crown.
Examine the rooted crown for annual lifespan and isolate an actual mature fertile floret with apical marginal hairs. Compare C. verticillata's separated tiers.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. virgata often has a single terminal digitate fan of feathery racemes, while verticillata has well-separated tiers and may form a tumbling mature head. C. cucullata has shorter crowded whorls and the strongly inflated sterile hood. Fertile-lemma apical hair crown, awn and annual crown are needed for confident C. virgata.
comparisons.cautions: Do not certify county nativity from a disturbed-site iNaturalist observation; do not infer identification from digitate head or color alone.
